grade_rationale.text: Afanasyev records the Моровая дѣва for the Poles (two-wheeled cart), sets a Lusatian tale of an invisible death-chariot beside it, and states that the Bulgarians count her among the samodivas and yuda-samovilas: three peoples in one compiler.
Afanasyev's 1865 and 1869 volumes are one source.
Ralston gives the Polish Pest Maiden story citing Wojcicki's Polish legends, not Afanasyev, so on this passage he is an independent second source.

Two independent authors and three peoples (Poles, Bulgarians, Sorbs) meet the widely-attested definition; only the Polish attestation is independently doubled, the Bulgarian and Sorb rows rest on Afanasyev alone.
